runtime.serving_boundary: one Node.js process for HTTP, SQLite queries, analytics, and deterministic matching; Python is offline-only; do not deploy a separate ML service

features.policy: Include only the consistent (approved_aliases, curated) and (exact_only, curated_exact_only) policy/status pairs from both job_skills and skills; exclude needs_review, needs_owner_review and all policy/status mismatches; show counts and denominator; never call observed prevalence hiring probability.
Normalize case and outer whitespace only; keep punctuation and semantic variants distinct until reviewed taxonomy exists.

Deterministic, explainable Node.js baseline; no trained model or external inference; label as skill overlap, not suitability or hiring probability; show evidence counts, return an empty result when no candidate profiles match, and never persist or log user input.
Use merged_tech_jobs for both cohorts; list missing country labels; disclose unverified source date semantics; do not imply representativeness.
Only explicit 2023 posted_at from international_jobs; never treat mixed updated fields as posted dates or current trends.
Keep disabled until comparable target, currency, period, provenance, sample size, validation and uncertainty reporting are approved.
Do not train or serve against incompatible and unreviewed source labels; first define and annotate a defensible taxonomy.

No model artifact or user-facing labels; remains offline/report-only. Any future Node.js-serving model requires a new approved decision, task-specific evaluation, and human review; no separate ML service is in scope.
All imported listing statuses are unknown_not_verified; never claim a listing is active or open.
Resource links and cost/access must be rechecked per item before publication; do not trust verification dates beyond the archive build date.
